newsitem.title: USA: Triarc sees nearly $1 bln in 1997 sales.
newsitem.headline: Triarc sees nearly $1 bln in 1997 sales.

text.p: Triarc Cos Inc said Wednesday that it expects 1997 sales to approach $1 billion, led by revenues from its Arby's restaurants and sales of its Snapple, Mistic and Royal Crown soft drinks.

The company said 1997 revenues will also include sales of specialty dyes and chemicals through its C.H. Patrick division of about $70 million and a portion of the $150 million in projected sales from National Propane Partners LP, in which the company has an equity stake.
Triarc bought the Snapple line from Quaker Oats Co for $300 million in a deal that closed late last month.

Snapple's 1996 sales totaled $550 million, down eight percent from 1995. Before the addition of Snapple, Triarc's beverage group, previously consisting only of Royal Crown and Mistic Brands, had 1996 sales of $310 million.
Quaker Oats bought Snapple two-and-a-half years ago for $1.8 billion and has lost money on it ever since. Quaker recorded a $1.1 billion write-off charge in its first quarter on the Snapple business.
